evidence: Abstract: "This paper aims to contribute to research efforts to improve the success of university nanosatellite missions using Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) to facilitate the initial project management and design phases."
Section 1: the paper aims to provide MBSE "including the initial phases of preparation, management, and analysis, tailored for university projects carried out by cohorts of students."

RQ1: Provides an ECSS/NASA-tailored SysML framework with lifecycle views, mission-analysis process flows, PBS/WBS/CBS derivation, requirements/structure/behavior packages, and MASAT1 examples.
Supports general nanosatellite mission/system modeling more than minimal-behavior modeling; prior knowledge is organized through needs, ConOps, requirements, and product tree rather than eliminated.
RQ2: Claims MBSE improves reliability, traceability, consistency, communication, planning, and project-document development, but evidence is mainly conceptual and single-case artifact demonstration.
Includes power-system architecture and verification trace examples but no EPS-specific reliability/reproducibility/integrability metric, baseline, or test/flight evidence.
RQ3: Shows requirements-in-the-loop/virtual verification links: operational requirement 100.1.6 satisfied by Power System and verified by LEOP Flow/Bus System Activation state machine.
Does not report complete EPS verification procedures, executable checks, SIL/HIL, or physical pre-development validation results.
